details: The US Treasury has temporarily lifted sanctions on Iranian crude oil production, sale, and transport until August 21, 2026, citing Tehran's commitment to "free and open transit" in the Strait of Hormuz and allowing IAEA inspectors. This move follows reports of progress in US-Iran negotiations aimed at a comprehensive deal within 60 days, initially easing global market concerns and leading to a drop in oil prices.
title: US Lifts Iran Oil Sanctions as Talks Progress, Easing Market Fears

details: The U.S. Federal Reserve, under its new Chair Kevin Warsh, has maintained interest rates but adopted a more hawkish stance, signaling potential rate hikes later in the year to combat persistent inflation. This shift towards a data-dependent, less predictable central bank, coupled with high Treasury yields, is draining liquidity from non-yielding risk assets like Bitcoin and increasing market volatility.
title: Fed's Hawkish Tone on Inflation Weighs on Crypto Markets

details: Bitcoin is exhibiting an increased correlation with U.S. tech stocks and other risk assets, making it more susceptible to traditional market volatility. Geopolitical developments, changing interest rate expectations, and global liquidity conditions are now rapidly influencing crypto prices, indicating Bitcoin is behaving more like a mature macro asset rather than an uncorrelated hedge.
title: Bitcoin's Correlation to US Stocks Strengthens Amid Macro Shifts

details: The STRC stablecoin has experienced a significant de-pegging from its $100 par value, falling to record lows and prompting scrutiny of its capital-raising design. This incident, while not directly compared to past major stablecoin collapses, raises concerns about liquidity stability and investor confidence in similar structured digital asset products, contributing to a broader "risk-off" sentiment in the crypto market.
sourceName: MEXC News (as reported by Crypto Breaking News)
title: STRC Stablecoin De-Pegging Sparks Liquidity and Confidence Fears
